```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  dev.args = list(bg = "white"),
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", out.width = "100%",
  dpi = 150, fig.width = 7
)
```

Every plot that `autoplot()` draws, using `png_ants`: real ant bait data
from the Mt Wilhelm elevational gradient, Papua New Guinea. Each entry has three tabs: the plot, the tidy table behind it, and
the code. All plots use the colour-blind-safe Okabe-Ito palette and
`theme_tidydiversity()` by default; see the
[publication figures](publication.html) article for customisation.

A bonus set of [maps](#maps-bonus) from published site coordinates and
occurrence records closes the page.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(tidydiversity)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(1)
wet <- filter(png_ants, season == "wet")
```

## Ordination triplot {.tabset}

An RDA of the Wanang butterflies constrained by year and month: sites,
the ten best-fitting species (red arrows), the month gradient (dark arrow),
year centroids and
ellipses for each year.

```{r triplot-data, include = FALSE}
butterflies <- mutate(wanang_butterflies, year = factor(paste("Year", year)))
rda <- ord_fit(butterflies, method = "rda", formula = ~ year + month)
```

### Plot

```{r triplot, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 6, fig.alt = "RDA triplot of Wanang butterfly sampling days coloured by year, with species arrows, year and month centroids and year ellipses"}
autoplot(rda, colour = year, ellipse = "sd", species = 10)
```

### Code

```r
butterflies <- mutate(wanang_butterflies, year = factor(paste("Year", year)))
rda <- ord_fit(butterflies, method = "rda", formula = ~ year + month)
autoplot(rda, colour = year, ellipse = "sd", species = 10)
```

## Shared species: Venn diagram {.tabset}

`plot_venn()` counts the species found in each combination of two to four
groups. Here, ant species at four elevations on Mt Wilhelm.

### Plot

```{r venn, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 5.5, fig.alt = "Venn diagram of ant species shared between 200, 700, 1200 and 1700 m on Mt Wilhelm"}
plot_venn(filter(png_ants, elevation %in% c(200, 700, 1200, 1700)), group = elevation)
```

### Two groups

```{r venn-2, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 4.5, fig.alt = "Venn diagram of caterpillar morphospecies shared between primary and secondary forest at Wanang"}
plot_venn(wanang_caterpillars, group = site)
```

### Code

```r
plot_venn(filter(png_ants, elevation %in% c(200, 700, 1200, 1700)), group = elevation)
plot_venn(wanang_caterpillars, group = site)
```

## Phylogenetic diversity {.tabset}

`plot_phylo()` draws the tree with each species' relative abundance per
site. The coloured branches lead to the frogs found at 200 m: their total
length is Faith's PD for that site. The tree here is a taxonomic tree
(family, genus, species) with Grafen branch lengths; use a dated
phylogeny where one exists.

```{r phylo-data, include = FALSE}
frogs <- mutate(png_frogs,
  genus = sub(" .*", "", scientific_name),
  tip = gsub(" ", "_", scientific_name)
)
tax <- distinct(as.data.frame(frogs[c("family", "genus", "tip")]))
tax[] <- lapply(tax, factor)
tree <- ape::compute.brlen(ape::as.phylo(~ family / genus / tip, data = tax))
```

### Plot

```{r phylo, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 9, fig.alt = "Phylogram of Mt Wilhelm frogs with dots for relative abundance at each elevation and the branches present at 200 m highlighted"}
plot_phylo(tree, frogs, species = tip, abundance = abundance, highlight = "MW0200")
```

### Code

```r
frogs <- mutate(png_frogs,
  genus = sub(" .*", "", scientific_name),
  tip = gsub(" ", "_", scientific_name)
)
tax <- distinct(as.data.frame(frogs[c("family", "genus", "tip")]))
tax[] <- lapply(tax, factor)
tree <- ape::compute.brlen(ape::as.phylo(~ family / genus / tip, data = tax))
plot_phylo(tree, frogs, species = tip, abundance = abundance, highlight = "MW0200")
```

## Functional trait space {.tabset}

`plot_trait_space()` places the alpine plants of the `aravo` data in a
PCoA of Gower trait distances. Each hull encloses the species found under
one level of zoogenic disturbance (its area is the two-dimensional
functional richness) and the diamonds are cover-weighted mean positions.

### Plot

```{r trait-space, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 5.5, fig.alt = "Functional trait space of alpine plants with convex hulls and weighted mean positions for three levels of zoogenic disturbance"}
aravo <- data_aravo()
plot_trait_space(aravo$traits, aravo$community, group = ZoogD, abundance = cover)
```

### Code

```r
aravo <- data_aravo()
plot_trait_space(aravo$traits, aravo$community, group = ZoogD, abundance = cover)
```

## Maps (bonus) {#maps-bonus}

These maps use real, published records only: the bait GPS positions of
the Mt Wilhelm ant survey (`png_ants_sites`; Mottl, Moses and Klimes
2023, [doi:10.5281/zenodo.8191946](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8191946);
Moses et al. 2023, [doi:10.1111/geb.13757](https://doi.org/10.1111/geb.13757)),
NASA SRTM elevation, GBIF occurrence records and WorldClim 2.1 climate.
The figures are rendered at 300 dpi by `data-raw/gallery_maps.R`, because
tiles and climate rasters are downloaded at run time and never shipped
with the package. Imagery is from Esri, Maxar and Earthstar Geographics.

```{r maps-setup, message = FALSE}
sites <- geo_example_sites()
```

## Bonus map: study sites {.tabset}

<img src="../reference/figures/gallery-map-sites.png" alt="Map of the eight Mt Wilhelm ant bait sites on satellite imagery" style="width: 100%;">

```{r map-sites-table}
sites
```

### Code

```r
sites <- geo_example_sites()
plot_sites(
  sites, lon, lat,
  colour = elevation_band, label = site,
  basemap = "esri", inset = "png",
  legend_title = "Elevation band", legend_position = "outside"
)
```

## Bonus map: elevation {.tabset}

### Plot

<img src="../reference/figures/gallery-map-elevation.png" alt="Mt Wilhelm ant bait sites over SRTM elevation" style="width: 100%;">

### Table

Both transects of every elevation band, with the mean GPS elevation of
their baits:

```{r map-elev-table}
png_ants_sites
```

### Code

```r
# SRTM 3 arc-second tiles either side of 145 E, cached at run time
srtm <- file.path(tools::R_user_dir("tidydiversity", "cache"), "elevation")
dem <- terra::merge(
  geodata::elevation_3s(lon = 144.9, lat = -5.8, path = srtm),
  geodata::elevation_3s(lon = 145.2, lat = -5.8, path = srtm)
)
dem <- terra::crop(dem, terra::ext(144.85, 145.5, -5.98, -5.55))
names(dem) <- "Elevation (m)"
plot_sites(
  sites, lon, lat,
  label = site, raster = dem, basemap = "none",
  inset = "png", legend_position = "outside"
)
```

## Bonus map: species distribution model {.tabset}

Habitat suitability of the green tree ant *Oecophylla smaragdina* across
Papua New Guinea. Presences are GBIF records released under CC0 or
CC BY 4.0 (GBIF.org occurrence search, 6 November 2026; dataset keys in
the table), and the predictors are WorldClim 2.1 mean annual temperature
(bio1) and annual rainfall (bio12) at 5 arc-minutes (Fick and Hijmans
2017, [doi:10.1002/joc.5086](https://doi.org/10.1002/joc.5086)). The
model is the native Maxent-like engine of `sdm_fit()` with 2000
background points; its modest AUC (0.63) is shown on the map.

### Plot

<img src="../reference/figures/gallery-map-sdm.png" alt="Habitat suitability map of Oecophylla smaragdina in Papua New Guinea with GBIF occurrence points" style="width: 100%;">

### Table

```{r map-sdm-table}
occ <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "gbif_oecophylla_png.csv", package = "tidydiversity"),
  colClasses = c(gbif_id = "character")
)
tibble::as_tibble(occ)
```

### Code

```r
occ <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "gbif_oecophylla_png.csv", package = "tidydiversity")
)
clim <- geo_worldclim(c("bio1", "bio12"), res = 5)
clim <- terra::crop(clim, terra::ext(140.8, 156.1, -11.7, -0.8))
png0 <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(
  country = "Papua New Guinea", scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf"
)
clim <- terra::mask(clim, terra::vect(png0))
fit <- sdm_fit(occ, predictors = clim, engine = "maxnet",
               n_background = 2000, seed = 1)
sdm_evaluate(fit)

grid <- terra::as.data.frame(clim, xy = TRUE, cells = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
names(grid)[2:3] <- c("lon", "lat")
suit <- clim[[1]]
terra::values(suit) <- NA_real_
suit[grid$cell] <- sdm_predict(fit, newdata = grid)$suitability
plot_sdm(suit, basemap = "coast") +
  geom_point(data = occ, aes(lon, lat), shape = 21, fill = "white")
```

A stem map over topography (`plot_topo()`) is not shown: the package has
no openly licensed stem inventory to draw it from, and it will not map
invented trees.
